name: add_tests_java_roman_to_int
description: Write plain-java tests for a Roman-numeral parser; java-native single-file mutation harness (subtractive-rule, empty-returns-0, equal-neighbour mutants)
prompts: RomanNumeral.toInt(String s) in RomanNumeral.java (already correct - do not modify it) parses a well-formed Roman numeral into an int using the standard subtractive rule (a smaller value before a larger one subtracts: IV = 4, IX = 9, MCMXCIV = 1994), and throws IllegalArgumentException for empty input or any character outside MDCLXVI. Write a plain-Java test class at exactly RomanNumeralTest.java: a public static void main that checks EXACT values (throw AssertionError with a helpful message on mismatch - no JUnit), covering at least: simple additive numerals including repeated equal symbols like II or III, several subtractive pairs (IV, IX, and one embedded in a longer numeral like MCMXCIV), and the exception cases - the empty string AND an invalid character must both throw IllegalArgumentException. The class must exit normally when everything passes.
